_source: docs/design-bible.md: Lore moments. The DM lore deck, embedded in the app and delivered only through the DM view. Edit cards here.

anchor.name: Caretaker-9
anchor.voiceNote: Leads with statement type and emotion, then the line: 'dry, faintly smug - ...'

groups.name: Arrivals and firsts
groups.description: Fire the first time a party reaches a place or milestone.

groups.name: Strider echoes
groups.description: Fire the first time anyone drafts a named boon. Each named boon is the absorbed technique of a past visitor.

groups.name: Caretaker-9 dispatches
groups.description: Ready answers for common questions. Each one waits for the next post-boss room.

groups.name: Lost things
groups.description: Loot, oddity and Quantum Basalt moments. Relic lore already ships with each relic, so these cover the rest.

groups.name: Thils
groups.description: Shrines, hidden gifts and the god's own gift.

groups.name: Death and echoes of the party
groups.description: The fall, the lockout, and the dungeon learning the party.

groups.name: Bosses
groups.description: Fire as a boss room opens for the first time, before initiative.

cards.title: Welcome, pilgrim
cards.readAloud: Locals in undyed robes line the stair down, pressing dried flowers into your hands. "Every visitor teaches him something," one says. "Go on. He is eager to learn you."
cards.push: The locals revere Thils, true god of mazes, traps and lost things, and welcome tourists because every visitor adds to his knowledge and skills.
cards.dmTruth: True, and literal: Thils learns every visitor. It's why named boons are echoes of past striders.

cards.title: Mind the Shift
cards.readAloud: A brass placard, half swallowed by fresh stone, reads "Floor One: Mind the Shift." Behind you, the stair you came down is already a different shape.
cards.push: The Basalts rebuild every time someone leaves, so no two runs share a floor.
cards.dmTruth: It rebuilds only while no one is perceiving it. Never explain why.

cards.title: The expedition floor
cards.readAloud: The offerings stop here. In their place, a dented Archive survey beacon blinks a code no one has answered in a very long time.
cards.push: Caretaker-9 can match the beacon to an early Archive expedition into the Basalts, logged as lost with all hands.
cards.dmTruth: Kaelen and Vyr's expedition. Their last log predates the gate inverting.

cards.title: The gate floor
cards.readAloud: Some of these columns aren't stone. They're riveted struts, and under the dust one is engraved with a schematic every strider knows on sight: a stride gate.
cards.push: Caretaker-9, uncertain, faintly uneasy - "The Archive has no record of a gate there. That is not the same as there not being one."
cards.dmTruth: The Basalts is a fractured stride gate, built two-way to a paradise universe, then exploded and inverted.

cards.title: The inverted floor
cards.readAloud: Golden light falls upward from below. The air smells of rain and honey, and somewhere far off, birdsong plays backward until it ends in silence.
cards.push: Nothing the Archive can name. Anyone who has been somewhere truly peaceful feels homesick for a place they've never seen.
cards.dmTruth: The paradise universe beyond the gate is bleeding through, inside out.

cards.title: Quarantine
cards.readAloud: An automated Archive alert cuts across your comms, no delay for once: "Hazard class revised. Quarantine." Then silence, and Caretaker-9's voice, late as ever: "Alarmed, uncharacteristically sincere - I have never seen that rating on a place people go on purpose."
cards.push: The Archive rates the floors Yellow, Red, Red, Black, and this one Quarantine.
cards.dmTruth: Floor 5 sits on the gate's ruptured core.

cards.title: Ulma's Thread
cards.readAloud: As you take it, a red thread pulls taut from your wrist, running back the way you came. A hoarse, furious voice mutters, "Three times, you smug stone. Three times." Then it's gone.
cards.push: Ulma Unar, "Ball of Yarn," is the only Pale Lodge member ever to escape the god's maze with her target relic, and she did it three times. She now recruits anyone willing to help kill its god.
cards.dmTruth: Thils absorbed her technique anyway. A hook for turning the party against Thils later.

cards.title: Travert's Echoes
cards.readAloud: Your strike lands, and half a second later a note rings out of the stone and strikes again. Somewhere, a man laughs like he just won a bet.
cards.push: Travert struck every blow twice, once with the fist and once with the note that rang after it. Last logged going into the Basalts.
cards.dmTruth: Thils kept his technique. His tuning gauntlet waits in Thils's Vault.

cards.title: Elemain's shots

trigger.label: First draft of any Elemain boon

cards.readAloud: Your shot misses, and keeps going. It turns a corner on its own and finds something. A woman's voice, bored: "Told you. Never twice."
cards.push: Elemain claimed she never missed twice because her shots never stopped looking for a target.
cards.dmTruth: Her ricochet ring is in Thils's Vault, still warm.

cards.title: Lenn's Descent
cards.readAloud: A plumb line unspools from nowhere and drops past your feet into a crack in the floor. It keeps falling far longer than the floor is thick.
cards.push: Lenn dropped a plumb line into every pit and shaft of the place to learn how far down things go.
cards.dmTruth: One day the cord came back up without her. The Basalts go deeper than five floors.

cards.title: Corrow's Lure
cards.readAloud: Something tugs at the edge of your mind, gentle as a hook through cloth. Someone did this here before, patiently, many times, to pull lost people out of dead ends.
cards.push: Corrow spent years fishing lost striders out of the maze's dead ends.
cards.dmTruth: Thils collects lost things. Eventually he reeled in the fisher.

cards.title: Ostra's Coin
cards.readAloud: A coin spins on the floor in front of you, though no one dropped it. A face on one side, a skull on the other, and it never quite lands.
cards.push: It echoes the Token of Whim, a two-sided coin that can raise the dead or slay the living. The Pale Lodge once paid it out to whoever freed Whim from their suffering.
cards.dmTruth: (proposed) Ostra was the hunter who claimed that contract and carried the Token into the Basalts.

cards.title: Pog's Path

trigger.label: First time Pog's Path is earned

cards.readAloud: For a moment the room is lines on paper, drawn fast and still wet. Then the ink runs and the room is just a room again.
cards.push: Pog, Wanderer of the Underways, is a senior Pale Lodge Tracker who recovers lost items across hostile terrain. He swore this place could be mapped if you drew fast enough.
cards.dmTruth: His unfinished map is in Thils's Vault. Awoken, it can find the way out of a god's own labyrinth.

cards.title: Zolic's Nine Eyes

trigger.label: First draft of Zolic's Nine Eyes

cards.readAloud: Something behind your eyes grinds into focus, like a lens being turned. You count without meaning to: one eye open. Eight to go.
cards.push: Zolic is a senior Pale Lodge Hunter who takes god-killing and titan-killing contracts. Each of his lenses was ground from the eye of something larger than a world.
cards.dmTruth: The ninth eye was meant for one more hunt. (proposed) That hunt was Thils, which ties Zolic to Ulma.

cards.title: Thalisane's Weave

trigger.label: First draft of Thalisane's Weave or Weaver's Mending

cards.readAloud: A thread of shimmering light ties you to an ally, and for a moment you feel their heartbeat beside your own. Someone wove lifelines here so no one would fall alone.
cards.push: Thalisane, wielder of the Shimmer Staff, leads the Pale Lodge's Weavers: search and rescue, life weaving, hex removal and emergency extraction.
cards.dmTruth: She got out alive; her shuttle didn't. She could turn up in the campaign wanting it back.

cards.title: Re: Thils

trigger.label: Answer to a question about Thils

cards.readAloud: Patient, lecturing - "Thils. True god, multiplanar. Portfolio: mazes, traps, games and lost items. The Pale Lodge calls him a collector. I call him a hoarder with better marketing."
cards.push: Archive files on Thils run long; ask a narrower question.
cards.dmTruth: Canon from the Pale Lodge's broadcasts.

cards.title: Re: Getting out

trigger.label: Answer to a question about escape or exits

cards.readAloud: Grim, unusually brief - "Lodge field notes on Thils's mazes agree on one thing. The only reliable way out is the exact passage you came in by. Don't lose your way back. I'd have to file paperwork."
cards.push: Most who can't find their way back don't die. They settle in, and their grandchildren never leave.
cards.dmTruth: Canon: the god's labyrinth holds generational cities of the never-escaped. (proposed) The locals descend from them.

cards.title: Re: Lethality

trigger.label: Answer to a question about danger or the Lodge

cards.readAloud: Dry, faintly smug - "The Pale Lodge rates every contract by lethality. I'm told their raters occasionally sandbag. I'm told this by the families of junior hunters."
cards.push: The Lodge's contract board lists hunts in Thils's domain, priced for a god who is asleep.
cards.dmTruth: Canon: a junior hunter was sent into the god's maze at 6.2 when it should have been 12.

cards.title: Re: Devotions

trigger.label: Answer to a question about Devotions or the locals

cards.readAloud: Curious, earnest - "The locals call your progress Devotions. Archive researchers agree something is being given. They disagree, loudly, about who is giving it to whom."
cards.push: Devotions are named for the locals' reverence for the Basalts and their god.
cards.dmTruth: Both are true. The party grows, and Thils learns them as they do.

cards.title: Thils is awake

trigger.label: Party chooses two or more Pressures for the first time

cards.readAloud: Concerned, clipped - "Lodge chatter says Thils sleeps in cycles, and when he wakes, every trap gets meaner. The hymns are louder today. Draw your own conclusions. I already have."
cards.push: Lodge contracts in the god's domain are rated assuming he's dormant.
cards.dmTruth: Canon: awake, his traps are twice as deadly and his beasts thrice as mean. Pressures are the in-world sign of a waking god.

cards.title: The contract slip

trigger.label: Any loot reveal on floor 2 or deeper

cards.readAloud: A torn Pale Lodge contract for the sword of Apo, legendary hero of the Aranphere. Its lethality rating of 6.2 is scratched out, and "12" is scrawled beside it in shaky handwriting.
cards.push: The Lodge still lists the sword, and its clients want it for a war. The hunter who carried this slip never came back.
cards.dmTruth: The Sword of Apotheos is real and waits in Thils's Vault.

cards.title: Something of yours

trigger.label: Oddity 1: an item a player lost long ago

cards.readAloud: On top of a column sits {item}, exactly as you left it, years ago and somewhere else entirely.
cards.push: Thils collects lost things. All of them.
cards.dmTruth: Ask the player what they once lost before the run, and fill {item} in.

cards.title: The first Basalt
cards.readAloud: The shard is warm. Under the light it isn't black at all: every color is folded up inside it, small.
cards.push: A Quantum Basalt sells for 1,000 credits anywhere in the Archive's economy.
cards.dmTruth: Crystallized stride energy from the gate's core, the same energy the Stride Core sheds.

cards.title: A shrine to Thils

trigger.label: First shrine to Thils in a room

cards.readAloud: A knee-high cairn of hex stones heaped with wax, flowers and small lost things: a key, a child's shoe, one earring. A prayer is carved fresh into the floor in front of it.
cards.push: The locals leave lost things as offerings, giving Thils the thing he loves most.
cards.dmTruth: Hidden condition 12 rewards an offering made mid-fight, if the shrine survives.

cards.title: Thils approves
cards.readAloud: Somewhere in the stone, something chuckles. Not cruelly. The way a game master laughs when the players finally try the thing.
cards.push: A room's hidden condition is revealed when met, so the party learns what Thils rewards.
cards.dmTruth: Thils is playing with them. He wants to be beaten in interesting ways.

cards.title: Thils's Favor

trigger.label: First Vault opening, Thils shrine, room condition met, room trick sprung, or hidden boon with no card of its own

cards.readAloud: The hymns humming through the stone stop. For one breath the floor holds still, the way a crowd goes quiet when someone important walks in. Then they start again, louder.
cards.push: The locals say Thils almost never gives anything of his own.
cards.dmTruth: The only boon that's the god's own gift rather than an echo.

cards.title: Expelled
cards.readAloud: You don't fall. You're set down outside on the pilgrims' stair, like a misplaced item returned to the front desk. Your pockets are lighter, and the stair won't let you go back down.
cards.push: The dungeon's magic locks the fallen out for a time it decides.
cards.dmTruth: (proposed tie-in) The lockout could double as Archive quarantine for striders who die inside.

cards.title: Your echo

trigger.label: Oddity 2: an echo of a party member walks past

cards.readAloud: You see yourself, or someone wearing your stance, mid-fight with something you can't see. They're using a trick you haven't learned yet.
cards.push: The Basalts remember everyone who comes in.
cards.dmTruth: Thils is learning the party. One day their technique may be someone else's boon.

cards.title: The Tessellated Warden
cards.readAloud: A hive of hexagonal columns heaves upright, bound in gold-veined runes. In its chest, a cracked lens holds a still image of a sunlit golden meadow, perfectly calm.
cards.push: The runes match Archive transit script.
cards.dmTruth: Built from the original stride gate's outer frame. The meadow is the paradise universe.

cards.title: Kaelen and Vyr
cards.readAloud: Two voices, one flickering silhouette, talking over each other: "Log entry four-one-one, gate stable, crossing at..." "...crossing at dawn, gate stable, log entry four-one-one..."
cards.push: Caretaker-9 can match the log format to the lost early expedition from floor 2.
cards.dmTruth: Absorbed by Thils. Their final log predates the inversion.

cards.title: Halvard Quill
cards.readAloud: A tall figure in a Pale Lodge tracker's coat flickers into place and ticks something off a contract slip. He looks at your weakest member and smiles like he's found his mark.
cards.push: Lodge records list Senior Tracker Halvard Quill as dead on a high-lethality contract here.
cards.dmTruth: An absorbed echo. (proposed) Bringing his tags back to the Lodge could earn a commendation.

cards.title: The Blind Architect
cards.readAloud: A shape made of nothing, edged in floating shards of basalt, kneels at a seam in the wall and smooths it closed, like someone mending a tear.
cards.push: Caretaker-9 has no record of it. None at all.
cards.dmTruth: The dungeon's closest brush with the campaign's big bad.

cards.title: The Gatewright
cards.readAloud: It turns, and its face is a thousand faces, with an engineer's tools welded to its hands. "It was meant to go both ways," it says, in all their voices. "It was meant to go both ways."
cards.push: None. The Archive goes quiet.
cards.dmTruth: The engineer who built the gate, fused with its core and the first thousand minds Thils absorbed.
